title: Preventing Redis Big-Key Event Loop Freezes
prompt: Your Redis 7 primary serves 85,000 OPS at 0.8ms p99 latency. A feature-flag/catalog cache stores 2.5 million entries inside a single Redis Hash (`catalog:items`, ~480 MB RSS). Whenever a daily refresh job runs `DEL catalog:items` or its 24-hour TTL expires, all clients experience 820ms-1,200ms latency spikes, triggering 200ms SocketTimeoutExceptions and cascading application retries. Redesign the invalidation mechanism and data layout so cache refreshes and expirations never stall the Redis event loop above 2ms.

spark.summary: Deleting or expiring a 480 MB Redis Hash with 2.5M fields via synchronous DEL blocks Redis's single-threaded aeMain event loop for 820ms while jemalloc frees millions of allocations, causing fleet-wide client timeouts.
spark.keyTakeaway: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, replace DEL with async UNLINK, enable lazyfree-lazy-expire/eviction, and shard multi-million-entry collections into 64 hash buckets (< 8 MB each) or delete in 500-field HSCAN+HDEL batches.

explanation.core:
